title: CV evidence — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, a project needs a concise CV line. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud one line about this project that a recruiter could verify, and cut everything they could not.

vocabulary.meaning: a claim tied to an artefact or a number a reader could go and check, rather than to an adjective
the part of a result you personally caused, distinguished from what the team or the tooling produced

expectedElements: The claim is tied to a checkable artefact or number
The personal contribution is distinguished from the team's
No adjective carries the weight of the claim
modelAnswer: The line I would keep is the one a recruiter could check. So: reduced the order listing from eight seconds to under two hundred milliseconds by removing a query per row, with the regression test that keeps it there. That names the problem, what I did, the measured outcome, and where the evidence lives. What I would cut is anything with an adjective doing the work, and anything the team did that I would be borrowing. If someone else designed the fix and I implemented it, the line says implemented, not designed. Do you want the artefact link in the line itself?
commonMistakes: Letting an adjective carry a claim that no artefact supports
Attributing a team or tooling outcome to yourself
variants: Answer again for a project where no measurement was taken.
